title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_302.txt
concise_summary: PKD engages in a phenomenological dialogue with God about the March 1974 visionary experience. Using infinite regress as a proof method, he explores whether the revelation came from God or Satan, trying to construct theories that explain 2-3-74 while God repeatedly demonstrates that all explanations lead to infinity—establishing infinity as the signature of divinity. He concludes that Satan's delusional world-construction ultimately led him toward truth through the exhaustion of rational frameworks.
key_claims: Every conceivable explanation for 2-3-74 generates infinite regress in thesis-antithesis dialectics, proving that infinity is the mark of God's presence
Pantheism is false; God is transcendent and separate from the material flux world, though fragmented traces appear within it
The suffering permitted by theodicy is justified because the bliss PKD experienced in 1974 was infinite and thus could only originate from a transcendent divine source
Statistical probability (counting which theories 'heap up' like computer punch cards) is the only epistemological method available when pure logic fails
Satan, by creating a sophisticated delusional world matching PKD's epistemological expectations, paradoxically led him toward God—an example of divine dialectical victory
PKD's exegesis itself has been futile and delusional, yet salvageable through recognition of the 'infinity route' as the singular reliable path

He tasted infinite bliss during that theophany, which he has never forgotten
For six and a half years (1974-1980) he has generated theory after theory each night and rejected each the next morning
He has created a 10-volume meta-novel (likely referring to VALIS or related projects) encoding his epistemological expectations
He is exhausted and weary from the intellectual labor of exegesis
He threatens to 'play until I die of it' in continuing the game of interpretation

Rest/weariness (drawn from Herbert; physical exhaustion as symptom of limitation)
On-Off, Yes-No, One-Zero, Yin-Yang (binary dialectics repeating infinitely)
tensions: PKD cannot know whether the 1974 voice was God or Satan, only guess on probabilistic grounds—a radical epistemic humility vs. his earlier certainty claims
He was led to truth by a delusional system (Satan's world), suggesting the boundary between delusion and revelation is unstable
His exegesis is simultaneously 'futile,' 'delusion,' and 'a hell-chore' yet also salvageable and pointed toward truth by its very infinity
God claims immutability ('Do I change?') while PKD's theories change constantly—but this could be a logical trick by a mimicking deity
PKD may himself be God (divided consciousness) or Krishna or Dionysus or Satan, with the game itself preventing him from knowing which role he plays
The 'only truth' PKD is allowed (probability, not certainty) seems to contradict the infinite bliss he claims as proof of God's reality

uncertainty_flags: The identity of the speaker in the dialogue is ambiguous: is it God, Satan, PKD's unconscious, or some other intelligence?
The exact nature and date of the 2-3-74 experience remain unresolved; only probabilistic certainty is claimed by the text itself
George Herbert quote attribution: the exact poem and date (1633) are given but should be verified (Dick may be paraphrasing or misremembering)
The 'ten volume meta-novel' is not named explicitly; it may refer to VALIS, Radio Free Albemuth, or an unpublished work
PKD's claim that 'by now it is evident' 6.5 years into theorizing assumes the listener accepts the infinite-regress logic, which is not self-evident
The concluding fragment breaks off mid-sentence, leaving the complete resolution unclear

I thought, then, an infinite number of explanations, in succession, that explained 2-3-74; each single one of them yielded up an infinite progression of flipflops, of thesis and antithesis, forever. Each time, God said, "Here is infinity. Here, then, I am." I tried for an infinite number of times; each time an infinite regress was set off and each time God said, "Infinity. Hence I am here." Then he said, "Every thought leads to infinity, does it not? Find one that doesn't." I tried forever. All led to an infinitude of regress, of the dialectic, of thesis, antithesis and new synthesis. Each time, God said, "Here is infinity; here am I. Try again." I tried forever. Always it ended with God saying, "Infinity and myself; I am here."
